title: Review signal catalog + quick mitigations (scratch)
content:
Notes to self — not polished. Purpose: capture signals I look for during reviews and quick mitigation actions I can propose in PR comments. Mix of heuristics, examples to copy/paste, and follow-ups.

Top-level signals (what I scan first)
- Surface-level safety check: does the change touch auth, KMS, or logging paths? If yes -> immediate security tag and SRE ping.
- Latency/Hotpath proximity: any change in request handling, batching, or cache key composition -> add perf benchmark note and small microbenchmark.
- Behavioral surface: CLI/SDK shape changes, defaults, or exported config names -> call out migration risk + deprecation plan.
- Test signal: new logic with no unit tests or change in existing test thresholds -> require at least one focused unit test and small integration simulation.
- Complexity spike: > 40 lines new function with nested conditionals -> suggest splitting, add TODO for docstring and examples.
- Third-party/dep additions: new transitive deps or heavier libs -> ask for risk rationale and license check.

Quick mitigation snippets (copy these into review comments)
- "Could you add a small unit test that demonstrates the new branch? A table-driven test covering the 3 edge cases would be ideal."
- "This looks like it touches a hot path — can you run `perf/baseline` before/after or add a simple benchmark in `bench/`? We should ensure 0% regression under typical batch sizes."
- "Consider extracting the inner loop into a helper and adding a focused docstring and small example. Makes future profiling/refactor easier."
- "Timeouts and retries: please document expected failure modes and default retry policy in the config struct — helps customers reason about behavior under overload."

Refactor ideas triggered by common patterns
- Repeated JSON encode/decode across handlers -> propose single marshal helper with pooled buffers (saves allocations).
- Conditional feature flags scattered -> centralize into `featuregate.go` with typed opts and a single validation step during startup.
- Ad-hoc metrics creation -> introduce `metrics.RegisterOnce` helper and call sites use static metric names. Reduces double-registration flakes in tests.

Canary / rollout play for risky PRs
- Add a toggle in config (env + console flag) default off.
- Deploy behind canary route (5% traffic) for 24–48 hours.
- Capture latency, error budget, token cost delta, and qualitative user-eval (small prompt set).
- If regression > 5% latency or increased error rate, rollback and open follow-up ticket with perf trace.

Checklist for merging (quick)
- [ ] Tests cover new paths + at least one failure case.
- [ ] Benchmarked hotpath if touched.
- [ ] Docs: config defaults and migration notes added.
- [ ] Metrics added / validated in staging.
- [ ] Add short changelog entry (internal) explaining behavioural change.

Unresolved questions / TODOs for me
- Decide standard wording for "needs benchmark" review comments so juniors copy it verbatim. Draft: "This touches a performance-sensitive area; please include a microbenchmark and perf run. See doc X for how we record bench outputs"
- Create small checklist template for security-affecting PRs and store in GH PR template.
- Follow up with Noelle about pooling helper she mentioned in retro (perf gains and caveats).

Random examples / snippets to paste in reviews
- Performance ask: "Run `go test -bench=.` under `./serving/` and paste the `Benchmark*` outputs; if you can't, add a TODO with expected numbers so we can gate later."
- Behavioral change flag: "This changes default behavior for users on v1.0. Please add a migration note and mark as opt-in behind `NEW_BEHAVIOR=true` for at least one release."

Last-minute thought: keep this file minimal and copy useful lines into a shared snippet doc later. For now, this is my personal fast-index for signals so I don't retype the same comment 30x.

End of scratch.
